name: Ganesh Consumer Products Ltd
title: Ganesh Consumer Products Ltd - 544528 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Atta volume loss from West Bengal ration-shop change cut FY27 revenue guide to about -5%, while EBITDA margin guided up 50-70 bps and H1 margin of 13% flatters a seasonally weaker H2.

capex.quote: They have since redirected their capacity towards selling atta in the unorganized segment, which has added to the competition in the open market.

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20.3% QoQ to INR2,267 million but fell 5% YoY on West Bengal atta disruption; EBITDA margin 13%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,267 million, up 20.3% QoQ and down 5% YoY, with B2C down 2.5% YoY almost entirely due to atta. Excluding atta, B2C grew 4.9% YoY and 26% QoQ. Operating EBITDA rose 23.6% YoY to INR295 million at a 13% margin (+302 bps YoY), helped mainly by lower other expenses from advertising phasing. PAT rose 68.7% YoY to INR188 million as finance costs fell to INR6 million. Management guided FY27 revenue down about 5% and EBITDA margin up 50-70 bps, with H2 margins structurally lower than H1.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR43 million a year ago

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balances incl. FDs
financial_highlights.value: INR1,082 million, of which INR425 million unutilised IPO proceeds

financial_highlights.change: vs 43 days in Q1; receivable days 6

financial_highlights.value: Close to INR7 crore in H1 per Q&A; 1.9% of revenue, in line with FY26

segments.name: B2C - atta
segments.commentary: Volumes declined after West Bengal stopped distributing atta via ration shops in May; NielsenIQ shows packaged atta in West Bengal down 6.3% YoY in the quarter. Displaced local millers now sell unbranded atta in the open market.

segments.name: B2C excluding atta
segments.commentary: Grew 4.9% YoY and 26% QoQ, which management calls the better read of underlying brand demand. E-commerce incl. quick commerce has a FY23-FY26 CAGR above 53%.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue down 13.8% YoY on lower service income and softer core product volumes.

segments.name: Spices
segments.commentary: Revenue grew strongly with margins improving on better realisations. YTD growth about 17-20%; management targets better-than-breakeven and double-digit FY27 growth on a FY26 base of about INR38-40 crore.

segments.name: Sattu
segments.commentary: Volumes grew more than 10% on the back of a Ravindra Jadeja campaign started in April; Bihar and Assam market doubled YoY from a small base.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue from operations expected to decline around 5% on atta pressure.
FY27 operating EBITDA margin expected to improve 50-70 bps YoY, i.e. about 10.5%-11%, per the CFO's clarification.
H2 EBITDA margin structurally lower than H1 because Rabi-crop raw material prices (wheat, gram, spices) firm up from late March/April; advertising to step up in H2.
FY28 margins expected to be similar to FY27 on a conservative basis; new snacks and sweets lines will absorb some of the margin gain.
Hyderabad plant sale (INR325 million, executed 1 October) to yield one-time gain of about INR199 million in Q3 FY27.
Management expects atta volumes to normalise in the medium term; FY28 outlook to be clearer by end of Q3 FY27.
capex_capacity: Bihar: long-term leased plot in Muzaffarpur from BIADA, possession taken and full amount paid; architect and consultant onboarded; civil work targeted to start around end-Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Assam: token amount paid for land; legal due diligence done; state approvals in progress; transaction expected post-Diwali.
Capital work in progress of about INR16 crore at September, mainly a sweets and snacks plant near Kolkata (being commissioned) and a bought-out corporate office in Salt Lake to move into next month.

Hyderabad plant (non-core, Johannesburg-based per transcript) sold for INR325 million, about 2.7x net worth; carrying value INR126 million; INR32.2 million advance held as current liability. Proceeds to be redeployed in Eastern India.
Sweets and snacks range (kaju barfi, besan ladoo, soan papdi, ethnic namkeens and bhujiya) to launch first in West Bengal across channels; ready-to-cook and instant mixes in development.
demand_pricing: Competition from unbranded atta sold by displaced flour millers in district markets is the main pressure; management is pursuing counter-strategies started 1 November.
Price hikes depend on competitors; management has enough stock to hold prices for now but will react to wheat price trends.
Earlier spice pricing was aggressive versus local players; management is raising realisations and may take price increases.
Value-added products are 62-65% of revenue this year; value-added margins are above wheat flour and whole wheat flour. Spices margin is above value-added per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for atta volumes and is a price hike likely given the wheat price trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Atta decline is the main B2C drag; volumes expected to improve in coming quarters. No price hike yet, depends on competitors, with enough stock held.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy for non-West Bengal regions?
qa_highlights.answer: Onboarding distributors and C&F agents in Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam and Bihar; e-commerce tie-ups in Bihar and Assam; Bihar plant planned for local wheat sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: How are spices growing and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations are being raised; spices YTD growth about 17-20%; management aims for better-than-breakeven and double-digit growth for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 outlook and margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early for FY28 revenue; clearer by end-Q3. Margins conservatively sustained, with some gain redeployed into snacks and sweets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the advertising spend numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 ad spend about 1.9% of revenue (about INR16 crore). H1 FY27 about INR7 crore; full-year to be in line with FY26, with H2 stepped up.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H2 margin expected to be lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Rabi-season raw material prices (wheat, gram, spices) are softer in H1 and firm up in H2; this is structural, and advertising will be planned rather than wasteful.

risks_watch: Continued atta volume erosion from unbranded millers in West Bengal and any extension of the state policy shift.
Rising wheat prices and whether competitors move on pricing; no price hike is currently planned.
H2 margin compression from seasonal raw material costs and a stepped-up advertising spend.
Execution timelines for Bihar civil work, the Assam land deal (post-Diwali), and the sweets and snacks launch.
Quality of the one-time gain (INR199 million) in Q3 and the reported cash conversion cycle versus the 32-day level.
B2B weakness (down 13.8% YoY) and a revenue decline of around 5% guided for FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability and balance sheet, but cautious on atta volumes. Management was vague on specific counter-strategies and did not give a price-hike decision or FY28 growth number, deferring these to Q3.
key_quotes: We believe the pressure on atta is temporary and expect the volumes to normalize in the medium term.
Excluding Atta, B2C revenue grew 4.9% year-on-year and 26% quarter-on-quarter, which is a better reflection of our underlying demand for our brands.
So, on an overall basis, it will be a bit early to comment because things are shaping up.
So it is structural, and obviously we'll not go ahead and bleed money by doing random advertisements.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue down about 5% on West Bengal atta disruption, with EBITDA margin up 50-70 bps to about 10.5-11%; ex-atta B2C grew 4.9% YoY, and backing rests on counter-strategies, the Kolkata sweets/snacks plant in trials, and spice realisations, with no firm order or capacity numbers for recovery.
